predecessors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
predecessors.text: Malwa, which the Pratapgarh inscription says Mahendrapala 'recaptured' in 945-946

predecessors.name: Rashtrakuta dynasty
predecessors.text: Malwa as a Rashtrakuta feudatory: 'Siyaka was a feudatory of the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III in his early days' (Harsola plates, 949)

successors.name: Khalji dynasty
successors.text: Malwa, after Ayn al-Mulk Multani, 'a general of Alauddin Khalji', killed Mahalakadeva in 1305

ledger.x: c. 1018: Bhoja takes Lata. 'Around 1018 CE, he defeated the Chalukyas of Lata'; the Bhoja page: 'Bhoja's first military aggression appears to be his invasion of the Lata region... around 1018 CE' and 'Bhoja subjugated the Chalukyas of Lata, whose ruler Kirtiraja may have served as his feudatory for a brief period'.…

c. 1040: Bhoja occupies Shakambhari. 'During the reign of Viryarama (r. c. 1040 CE), the Paramara king Bhoja invaded the Chahamana kingdom' and 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period'; the Bhoja page: he 'defeated and killed Viryarama'. Hatched, not annexed.
1056 (bridge): the Chahamanas are back at Shakambhari.
1056 (bridge): Lata falls to the Kalachuris after Bhoja's death.
1067: the plunder ends; no treaty named.
1111 (bridge): the south of Rajasthan passes to the Chaulukyas.

c. 1175-1178: Vindhyavarman restores Paramara power. 'accomplished this during the reign of the Chaulukya king Mularaja II (r. c. 1175 - c. 1178)' (R. C. Majumdar) and 'having regained control of the capital Dhara by 1192 CE'; A. K. Majumdar 'believes that Malwa remained under Chaulukya control during Mularaja's…

c. 1255 (bridge): the capital moves from Dhara to Mandapa-Durga (Mandu), 'after Dhara was sacked multiple times'. 'Either Jaitugi or Jayavarman II moved the Paramara capital': the page gives no year, so the change of reign, 1255, is used. Not on the Devapala page (it names neither Dhara nor Mandu); unchanged.

wars.name: Paramara sack of Manyakheta
wars.outcome: 'Around 972, Siyaka sacked the Rashtrakuta capital Manyakheta'; no Paramara land gain.

wars.name: Munja-Tailapa war
wars.outcome: Munja 'was defeated and killed by Tailapa some time between 994 CE and 998 CE'; the Paramaras lost territory south of the Narmada, which Sindhuraja then partly recovered after defeating Satyashraya (undated).

wars.name: Bhoja's wars of expansion
wars.outcome: Lata (c. 1018, from the Lata Chalukyas), northern Konkan (1018-1020, from the Shilahara vassals of the Western Chalukyas), Shakambhari (c. 1040); Konkan lost by 1055; Bhima I and Karna 'attacked his kingdom' about 1055 and the Kalachuris took Lata (ledger…

wars.name: Western Chalukya-Paramara wars
wars.outcome: After 1042 Someshvara I invaded Malwa and sacked Dhara; the Chalukyas plundered Paramara cities in 1058-1067; no annexation.

wars.name: Jayasimha Siddharaja's conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Dhara taken in 1135-1136; 'He defeated Naravarman after a 12-year campaign' (the Jain account, which the page treats with caution); Malwa annexed.

wars.name: Kumarapala-Ballala war
wars.outcome: 'The Chaulukya king Kumarapala defeated Ballala around 1150 CE.

wars.name: Vindhyavarman's recovery of Malwa
wars.outcome: Vindhyavarman restored Paramara power and held Dhara by 1192; 'defeated by the Chaulukya general Kumara at a place named Goggasthana' (undated).

wars.name: Yadava invasions of Malwa
wars.outcome: Simhana invaded in 1215, Krishna defeated the Paramara king before 1250 and Ramachandra in the 1270s: no territorial annexation recorded.

wars.name: Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Malwa
wars.outcome: Mahalakadeva killed in 1305 by Ayn al-Mulk Multani; Paramara rule lingered in north-eastern Malwa to about 1310.

certainty.note: No treaty line appears on any page opened; Bhoja's limits (Chittor, the Sabarmati, Vidisha, upper Konkan) are scholars' readings of inscriptions, and Dhara changed hands several times.
